items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: So they figured who’s the most important TV personality, black TV personality, Sammy Davis. He was on Johnny Carson all the time. So they got him to do it.

ctx.x: There’s always an answer. I’m glad you moved on, you brought up jingles, because I wanted to spend a little time with that. It seems like another area of music that requires a certain approach, especially if it’s background music. And did you find that difficult to get used to?

Very difficult. Especially 60-second spots. You have to say it in 60 seconds but you also have to be able to cut that 60 down to 30 or a 20, or make it longer. I’ll say one thing, I should point out that all the time I was writing jazz with, you know, two young boys, two children and a wife, the way you survive is writing whatever you can. And the jingles and the industrial videos and all that stuff saves your life. But — and you don’t have to put your name on it. So it was a great way of supporting a family, but…
Well the next time I go into Wegman’s I’m going to say I know the guy who did all your commercials.
